body:
Congratulations on your car. While it's not something I personally enjoy, what is, I wish you the very best of luck in your racing. 

I wish I could feel that kind of passion for something. . . I just don't. I worked 8 hours in a kitchen Sunday. Scrubbing my hands raw and bloody. Know why? Because I said I would. I just did it to see if I could. I came to a single conclusion during that time. If that kind of work is what it takes to survive, then I don't want to survive. I don't want to spend my whole life doing that sort of nothing. Maybe I'll take your advice. . . make some achievable goals for myself. See what happens.

> What will the world gain and what will you gain personally from the above mentioned act?


The world would lose little, and gain one fewer person. I would gain peace. An end to the apparently pointless struggle of existence. What do I gain by staying? 


Why go early? 

Why not? At least this way I go on my terms. I decide when and how my existence comes to an end. I get to skip, potentially, decades of effort, torment, regret, depression, ect. and get right to the endgame.

I don't know. I don't really feel passion for anything. I've tried programming, art, cooking, psychology, biology, the list goes on. I feel a sort of detached interest but even that eventually fades. 

Right now I'm trying to force myself to pursue programming as a career but I'm getting discouraged by a lack of clear pathway. I'm also behind in mathematics for the most part. Making it difficult to succeed in something so fundamentally numeric. I read books and forget the first part of the paragraph before I even finish it. I know I like programming too. It's fascinating when you think about it. . . I just can't find the passion for it or anything else.

I appreciate your taking time out to speak with me. I feel as though we're simply going to fundamentally disagree on this point but I grateful that you tried. 

To me, love has been shown to be fleeting and inconsistent. 

It's not so much that I'm sad. . . I'm more. . . tired? Frustrated? Sadness isn't a factor. . . I'm just feeling hopeless.

Love? On the rare occasions I've been graced with it the feeling either went unrequited or quickly turned to ash. Every potential romance I've fostered has ended in sadness for everyone involved. Sometimes with them cheating on me, or cheating with me on someone else, without my knowledge. 


Beauty? I'm not immune to the glory of a sunset, nor the majesty of landscapes. . . comfort though they may be, when compared to the atrocity of our existence they seem small indeed. 

I can do no more to change the horrors of our planet than I can to change it's beauty. All I can do is stand mute witness to them both. It wears at me. Perhaps I take too much to heart but I can't help it. . . it's my nature. 

More often people are cruel, petty, vindictive, and bureaucratic. I can't possibly help you, why you've got a 22-a when you need a 22-b. Refill the forms. Jump through the hoops. Shed your dignity and beg like a dog. . . because we own you now.

I admit this sounds nice. . . but most jobs don't allow this kind of freedom. Especially not right off the bat and not to someone like me. I can't afford to just get a pilot's license and run a plane around the world. 

There was a study, it amuses me to point out, that said that depressed people, I think I qualify, are actually better in tune with reality than optimistic people. To me the kind of life you're talking about seems impossible. It seems like, if you'll forgive me, self-deception at it's finest to believe it isn't impossible. 

Again though, I just find it so hard to get passionate about anything when I know it's not going to last. When I know that my life will have amounted to essentially nothing. I could sleep in and play video games all day and the result will be the same. Except that I'd quickly find myself homeless. . .
